title: Prefix Products: Product of Array Except Self
oneLiner: For each position, the product of every other element, without division: multiply the product of everything to its left by the product of everything to its right.
keyTakeaway: answer[i] = (product of nums[0..i - 1]) · (product of nums[i + 1..n - 1]). Fill answer with running left products in one pass, then sweep from the right multiplying in a running right product. Two passes, O(n), and O(1) extra space besides the output. No division, so zeros need no special cases.
explanation:
Return an array where answer[i] is the product of all elements of nums except nums[i], in O(n) time and without using division. [1, 2, 3, 4] gives [24, 12, 8, 6].

Dividing the total product by nums[i] is the obvious idea and the one that's ruled out, partly because zeros break it: with one zero, every other answer is 0 and the zero's own answer is the product of the rest; with two zeros, everything is 0. The prefix approach handles all of that without a single special case.

Split "everything except i" into "everything before i" and "everything after i". Those are prefix and suffix products, the multiplicative cousin of Prefix Sums. Pass 1, left to right: keep prefix = 1; set answer[i] = prefix, then prefix *= nums[i]. Now answer[i] holds the product of everything to the left. Pass 2, right to left: keep suffix = 1; multiply answer[i] by suffix, then suffix *= nums[i]. Now each answer[i] also includes everything to the right.

Two passes, O(n) time. Using the output array to hold the left products means only two running variables of extra space, O(1) (the output itself is usually not counted). Building separate left and right arrays first is a fine stepping stone at O(n) space.

The visualization runs [1, 2, 3, 4]: the array is answer after each step.

def product_except_self(nums):
    answer = [1] * len(nums)
    # TODO: pass 1, left to right: prefix = 1; answer[i] = prefix; prefix *= nums[i].
    # Pass 2, right to left: suffix = 1; answer[i] *= suffix; suffix *= nums[i].
    return answer

visualizationSteps.message: nums = [1, 2, 3, 4]. Pass 1 writes the product of everything to the left of each position.
answer[0] = left product 1. Then prefix *= 1 gives 1.
answer[1] = left product 1. Then prefix *= 2 gives 2.
answer[2] = left product 2. Then prefix *= 3 gives 6.
answer[3] = left product 6. Then prefix *= 4 gives 24.
Pass 2: answer[3] *= right product 1, giving 6. Then suffix *= 4 gives 4.
Pass 2: answer[2] *= right product 4, giving 8. Then suffix *= 3 gives 12.
Pass 2: answer[1] *= right product 12, giving 12. Then suffix *= 2 gives 24.
Pass 2: answer[0] *= right product 24, giving 24. Then suffix *= 1 gives 24.

recognitionSignals: "For each element, combine all the OTHER elements": split into a prefix part and a suffix part.
Division (or subtraction) is banned or breaks on zeros.
gotchas: Updating prefix before writing answer[i] includes nums[i] in its own product.
Starting prefix or suffix at 0 instead of 1 zeroes everything.
Dividing the total product fails when the array contains zeros.
confusableWith: Prefix Sums answers range-sum queries from one prefix array; here each answer combines a prefix with a suffix.
Trapping Rain Water also needs a left-side and right-side summary for each position (max height), computed by the same two sweeps.

complexity.note: Two passes over the array. Besides the output array (O(n), usually not counted), only the running prefix and suffix products are stored.

referenceSolutions.python:
def product_except_self(nums):
    answer = [1] * len(nums)
    prefix = 1
    for i in range(len(nums)):
        answer[i] = prefix  # product of everything left of i
        prefix *= nums[i]
    suffix = 1
    for i in range(len(nums) - 1, -1, -1):
        answer[i] *= suffix  # times the product of everything right of i
        suffix *= nums[i]
    return answer
